title: The Trapdoor
build: Cleveland Cracking Service disk, cracked by Ian

records.c: Upper bytes of eight times the tile index for indices 32–255. The bitmap blitter adds them to the high byte of the graphics base at $5610.
Reads another byte from the title music stream and uses it as the low operand of the jump at $1506. The jump selects an event handler within page $15.
Decodes one note for voice 1 before reading the duration.
Calls the voice 2 note routine, then reads the duration.
Calls the voice 3 note routine, then reads the duration.
Decodes a note for voice 1, then one for voice 2 before reading the duration.
Calls the note handlers for voices 1, 2 and 3 in order before reading the duration.
Six bytes set attack/decay for all three voices followed by sustain/release for all three.
Copies the saved stream start from $F3/$F4 into $F1/$F2. Next dispatch fetches the original first event again.
First byte sets the pulse state reset flag. The next three set the high pulse width bytes of the three voices and save copies in $1998–$199A.
Stores two stream bytes in $1987 and $199E. The duration routine uses them for the tick countdown and the secondary counter.
Reads three voice control bytes into $1980–$1982 and three related settings into $1984–$1986.
Zeros the three voice counters via Y and patches five immediate operands used to time or increment per-tick effects.
Increments the little-endian stream pointer $F1/$F2 and reads at the resulting address plus Y.
Resolves a pitch through $18A3, stores its SID frequency pair and updates voice 1 control.
Counts down $F0 and uses independent counters at $F7, $F6 and $F5 to schedule changes between events.
Reads the sequence through $F1/$F2. $FF returns immediately. When Y equals $F0 it goes to $1500 to start another sequence step, otherwise to $16ED.
Doubles the stream's pitch index and reads the resulting two bytes from $19B0. Returns the first in X and the second in A.
Takes another byte from the current stream. Zero goes straight to $1500. A nonzero count scales the delays in $F0 and $1988 using $1987.
Copies five arguments from the stream into $198B, $198C, $198E, $1989 and $198A in that order.
Copies three arguments from the stream into $198F–$1991.
Writes two stream bytes to $199C/$199D. The voice 2 update tests the first of them against Y at $1620.
Reads six pitch indices and patches the two operands in each of the three noise presets at $1943, $1950 and $195D.
Loads $03 and $04 into the voice 1 frequency step operands used at $1714 and $1720 before gating noise.
Loads $1D and $3B into the same voice 1 operands before gating noise.
Loads $4B and $5E into the same voice 1 operands before gating noise.
Clears voice 1 frequency and control, sets noise plus gate, and schedules the event duration.
Interleaved pairs read by $18A3. The first byte goes to SID's high frequency register and the second to its low register.
Saved loop start. The argument reader increments before loading, so $1A3A begins the first event. The first two commands are $E9 and $E6. The $57 at $1FE5 loops here.
Continuation of the event stream at $1A39, read through the restart event at $1FE5. The last note event at $1FE0 selects the three-voice handler.
Seven low bytes for the atlas bases. The compositor uses the nonzero tile set selected at $55FB.
Seven high bytes paired with $2000. Together the nonzero entries point to $2846, $3106, $200E, $254E, $2DDE and $357E.
Set 3 starts at $200E. Each tile stores eight successive bitmap rows. This span starts with tile 0.
Set 3 tile 128 starts here. The next graphics base is $254E, after 40 more eight-byte cells.
Set 4 starts here and runs to the base of set 1 at $2846, a distance of 95 eight-byte cells.
Set 1 starts with tile 0 here. The compositor adds the scaled tile index to this base when X is 1 at $5601.
Set 1 tile 128 starts here. The following set base is $2DDE, after space for 51 more cells.
Set 5 starts here and the set 2 base at $3106 is 101 eight-byte cells later.
Set 2 starts here. Its base is selected by X=2, using the pair at $2002 and $2009.
Set 2 tile 128 starts here. There is room for 15 cells before set 6 at $357E.
Set 6 starts here. The eight-byte lookup read by $564A begins 38 cells later at $36AE.
Eight indices used to get tile row bytes from the RAM table at $0600 when the alternative graphics branch runs.
The unpacker enters here. The jump bypasses the restart path at $3803 and goes to the initial hardware and title setup.
Copies the restart template through $3F46 and seeds six records 14 bytes apart with values from $C501.
Sets up the hardware, copies the initial template selected by X=$06, then calls the title and mode setup before entering the loop at $3868.
Samples input through $5127, then runs the routines at $3EE5, $3961, $6400, $3BEA and $3FBB before the display calls.
Installs RAM interrupt vectors, configures CIA1 timers and selects the VIC bitmap in bank $C000.
Saves A and the CPU port, exposes I/O to read CIA1's interrupt status and dispatches through $FFF8 only when bit 1 is set. Restores registers and the interrupted bank before RTI.
Jumps through the writable $FFF8 vector, which defaults to the RTS at $3936 and can be replaced by sound playback.
Four words copied to $FFF8–$FFFF. Hook and reset use $3936, NMI returns at $3955 and IRQ starts at $3937.
Chooses the pending creature or request slot through $11 when its flags allow, then waits for $55 to expire before entering the request selection or update path.
Writes type $0F, flags $1B and shape pointer $BAD1 to the first three records starting at $9A0D, using a 14-byte stride.
Counts down the byte at $3FB3, then updates the next pixel row across four cells of the anger bar. Every eight rows it moves to the preceding bitmap band.
Writes zero to three adjacent colour cells in each of 19 rows at the right side of the screen.
Split 21-entry address table for the bitmap bands of the anger bar. $3AAF reads the two halves using the band counter at $3B57.
Samples an index in 0–3 and tests the sign bit in the four-entry table at $C73F. When its search is exhausted, clears all four sign bits and resamples.
Draws 160 segments through $3AAF, then selects the custom glyph set at $C744 and sends the inline strip description at $3FAC to the text renderer.
Clears the work plane, sets the panel colour and draws glyph $04 along each run in the five-byte table at $3E69.
Twelve runs give column, row, count, horizontal step and vertical step. The first puts 40 copies of glyph 4 across row $15. $FF ends the list.
Waits for the $73 countdown, then compares the horizontal coordinate of the $9B33 object with $62/$63. The matching branches change the window by $20 or wrap the coordinate.
X selects a six-byte record at $3F88. It patches the source and destination operands and copies the selected block with a length split into a starting count and whole pages.
Six-byte records supply source, destination, low count and page count to the copy loop at $3F46.
Copies 104 bytes at $C508 to $0010 before setting up a new game.
Copies 462 bytes from $9981 back to the buffer at $C570. The entry at $3F88 copies the same extent the other way.
Tests the hint selector at $28. $FF returns, and the active path increments $3FBA, looks up the requested string and calls the display routine during its allowed interval.
Resets the display slot counter to 28 and draws a character from the selected hint.
Reloads the saved hint address and byte offset before drawing the following character.
Steps past characters until it consumes $5B or $26. Callers repeat it to index a group of hints and to select additional lines.
Clears the selected cell, banks in the character ROM and gets the row bytes. Maps the stored upper and lower case encodings to their ROM glyphs.
Calls $4257 for positions 29 down through 1 and reinitializes the hint position byte at $3FB5.
The opening bracket-delimited phrases include What next, Wait and Preparations. Later entries contain recipe advice such as Fetch a can and More worms.
This group begins with a control-prefixed phrase leading to Get me out of here. $3FE4 selects it directly before skipping entries according to $28.
Passes the list at $47FB to the same conditional message parser used for other responses.
List beginning with YOU SILLY SUICIDAL LITTLE BERK. The structural bytes precede the text and $2B separates words at line-break opportunities.
Reads a message list through $78/$79. Tags $21 and $29 test a state byte or introduce a RAM operand, and the fall-through tests a mask against $4E.
Copies the selected text to RAM at $CC00 until $24 introduces a substitution or $5D ends the text.
Advances the script pointer to the next $5B marker.
Starts formatting the selected line at screen address $C8F0 and looks up style values using the running display position.
Measures a word up to a dollar sign, plus sign or closing bracket. Uses half the remaining width to position the word before drawing it.
Reads one byte at a time from $CC00 until it reaches $24, $2B or $5D, the boundaries recognized by the centring routine.
Saves the doubled digit or letter index, or special punctuation index, for the row copy at $4CC9.
Index set by $4C47 and multiplied by eight to select the glyph rows.
Sixteen bytes per glyph. Indices $00–$09 are digits, and $0A–$0D are period, comma, apostrophe and exclamation mark. Letters A through Z occupy $11–$2A.
Three-byte JMP entries expose the rendering, input and audio services to callers.
Samples $D012 into the state bytes at $51FD–$51FF and makes the last sample odd.
Patches the immediate colour loaded by $520E, then falls through to its hardware write.
Saves the banking byte, exposes I/O, writes the colour operand at $520F to $D020, then restores the saved bank.
Starts at $9601 with RAM mapped in and selects records whose first byte is nonzero and nonnegative. $FF ends the scan.
Advances the object pointer at $86/$87 by 14 to the next record.
Increments the pass number at $81, restarts from the object list until the count reaches six, then banks I/O back in.
Reads an object's shape pointer from offsets 10–11, moves coordinates into drawing space and fetches commands from the resulting shape stream.
Dispatches $EE–$FF as shape commands. Lower values are tile indices. Within the 32 by 20 work grid it writes the bank, tile and style fields and advances the cursor.
Advances the stream pointer and patches the JMP operand from the split handler addresses, indexed by the opcode minus $EE.
Eighteen low address bytes followed by eighteen high bytes. $EE selects the handler at $537B.
Saves the next stream byte as the loop count and saves the subsequent pointer as the repeat start.
Decrements the saved repeat count and restores the saved pointer until it reaches zero.
Uses the bounded random routine to skip three bytes per selected alternative after the argument.
Passes the argument byte to the sound effect selection entry at $5112.
Writes the next shape byte to $71. While this is nonzero, cell records use the saved style instead of supplying a style byte.
Saves the next shape byte to $6F as the tile bitmap bank used by the cell writer at $52DA.
Clears the style override, restores the local drawing coordinates from $5A/$5B and returns.
Adds the two signed byte offsets to the drawing row and column.
Adds the two byte offsets and saves the resulting coordinates as the new origin as well as the current drawing position.
Saves the old pointer on the 6510 stack, recursively draws the stream named by the next address and resumes at the bytes after the call.
Takes the supplied shape branch when the $10 flag at $9B35 passes. Otherwise skips the two-byte pointer.
Increments a writable frame index, wraps at the following limit and jumps to the selected address in a table of address pairs.
Compares graphics cell records in the two work areas, skipping matching cells. Processes twenty rows and branches to the copy path when fields differ.
Fetches updated cell fields, maps the low six bits of its style byte to a screen colour byte and branches on the tile set and flags.
Adds the low and high parts of tile index times eight to the selected split bitmap base, then patches the copy source.
Copies eight consecutive bitmap rows from $90/$91 to $84/$85, taking Y from seven down to zero.
Uses the row indices at $36AE to fetch an eight-row tile from the byte lookup at $0600.
Sixty-four entries map the low six bits of a changed cell's style byte to the packed foreground and background nibbles written to the cell colour plane.
Chooses which half of the workspace to clear from the current page selection at $58, with I/O banked out.
Clears ten pages of RAM from $D600 through $DFFF. The callers bank I/O out before entering this loop.
Clears ten pages from $CC00 through $D5FF, including RAM underneath the hardware registers.
Initializes the key tables on first use, then reads the merged controls. A separate flag is handled by waiting for another input.
Converts the key codes at $5838 into row and column masks for the input scan.
The bytes X, Z, A, Q, C, T and H are passed through the matrix lookup at $583F during setup.
Seven active-low row masks synthesized from the bindings at $5838 and written to CIA1 port A.
Seven masks applied to CIA1 port B while testing the selected keys.
One action bit per binding. The first six correspond to right, left, down, up, drop and tip.
Scans seven keyboard bindings, reads active-low joystick port 2 and ORs their bits together. A nonzero result is saved in $7C.
Accumulator cleared before each scan. ORs in one action bit for each matching key matrix binding.
Uses character position and row tables to patch the destination, then copies eight glyph rows. With no custom font base, selects the C64 character ROM at $D800.
Pops the JSR return address, passes the following bytes to the text reader and jumps to the reader's updated pointer after the terminator.
Each text run starts with position and colour. $26 starts another run with new settings and $5D ends the stream.
Starts the title music, clears the display, selects the ROM font and invokes the inline text renderer.
Position and colour headers interleaved with text. Starts with R Redefine and S Start, then lists the direction keys, Drop, Tip and port 2.
Starts the title player and polls until the combined control sample is idle, then waits for an active input.
Repeats the CIA1 port B sample until stable, then folds in the low four joystick bits on CIA1 port A.
Saves the previous timer hook, installs $186E, sets SID volume to 15 and initializes two stream pointers to $1A39.
Enters the sound bank context, clears sound state and writes the resulting voice and filter settings to SID before restoring the caller's context.
Writes the three voice records spaced $37 apart, then updates the shared filter registers from the selected voice's state.
Writes frequency, pulse width and envelope registers for the voice selected by Y and combines four fields into the control byte.
Clears the bitmap work area from $E000 up through $FF3F and the four screen pages at $C800–$CBFF.
Calls ten update routines in a fixed order, starting at $641F and ending at $89D7.
Copies bytes from $9B37 and $9B3A–$9B3B to zero page. Preserves the cursor pair from $32/$33 across $644E using $30/$31.
Uses the object flags at $9B36 and then shifts the current control mask to find the first set bit. Patches the jump from the two tables at $649A and $64A2.
Eight destinations indexed by $644E. Index 0 is the idle path at $64AA, and indices 1 through 7 correspond to the control bits in order from least significant.
Clears bit 3 of Berk's flags and chooses an idle sequence at $AA44 or $AA24, or advances the existing actor sequence.
Chosen by control bit $10. Tests the carried-object flag and the current coordinate before entering the candidate-object path.
Chosen by control bit $20. Tests the carried-object flag and record state before loading an animation sequence.
Chosen by control bit $01. Probes the position with $9B38 decremented, then restores the coordinate before using the result.
Chosen by control bit $02. Checks an actor flag before querying the next position at $8510.

Chosen by control bit $08. Clears bit 1 of the actor flags before querying an object or boundary via $85DE.
Loads X and Y as a new actor sequence pointer. Fetches its first address pair and stores the shape bytes at offsets 10 and 11 of the current object.
Advances the actor sequence pointer by one two-byte entry before reading the new shape address.
A sequence entry with high byte zero treats its low byte as a command index and patches the destination from the tables at $8689 and $86DB.
Reads the count into $68 and saves the following sequence pointer in $64/$65.
Decrements $68 and either advances on expiry or restores the saved pointer in $64/$65 for another pass.
Split addresses for the actor command byte. The index comes from the low byte of a sequence entry with its high byte set to zero.
